paper.title: On learning Whittle index policy for restless bandits with scalable regret

settings.name_in_paper: Restless bandit, Model A (all arms yield rewards), Bayesian regret w.r.t. Whittle index policy
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Restless Markov bandit (MDP with n independent controlled Markov arms); markovian environments are out of scope in ontology v0.5.

settings.definition_quote: Restless bandits (RB) are a class of resource allocation problems where, at each time instant, a decision maker has to select $m$ out of $n$ available alternatives. Each alternative ... is a controlled Markov process ... Model A: All arms, whether active or not, yield rewards

settings.name_in_paper: Restless bandit, Model B (only active arms yield rewards), Bayesian regret w.r.t. Whittle index policy
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Restless Markov bandit (MDP with n independent controlled Markov arms); markovian environments are out of scope in ontology v0.5.
unmapped: n arms are controlled Markov chains with finite state spaces and unknown transition matrices; m of n arms activated each round
learner observes the full state of every arm
reward functions known; only active arms yield rewards in [0, R_max]
regret measured against the Whittle index policy of the true model
indexability of every arm assumed (Assumption 1); average-reward Bellman equation solvable (Assumption 2)
settings.definition_quote: Model B: Only the activated arms yield rewards. The state of the passive arms evolves, but the arms do not yield reward.

conditions: Assumption 1: every arm indexable for all theta
Assumption 2: average-reward Bellman equation has bounded solution

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Under Assumptions~\ref{assump:indexable}--\ref{assmp:3}, the regret of {\tt RB-TSDE} is upper bounded as follows: \REGRET(T; {\tt RB-TSDE}) < 40 \alpha \frac{R_{\max}}{1-\lambda^*} \bar {\mathsf{S}}_n \sqrt{T \log T}, where $\alpha = n$ for Model~A and $\alpha = m$ for Model~B.

results.notes: Model A case (alpha = n, n = number of arms mapped to K). Regret against Whittle index policy. Strict inequality.
